Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Payments is excited about Redwood. Our legal team is drafting the US privacy addendum (CCPA/CPRA + state analogs) and we wanted to confirm a few points before we circulate a redline:

1) Service provider designation — Can Redwood be contracted as a "Service Provider" (not a "Controller" or "Seller") for hosted inference where Redwood processes transaction-derived prompts for our product features? We need explicit language for the addendum confirming limited use and no "selling" of Personal Information.

2) Telemetry exports — Our SecOps team is concerned about operational telemetry that Redwood collects for debugging and platform health (request logs, IPs, user agent strings). We often need to export logs to our SIEM during incident response. Will Redwood permit a narrow "telemetry export" exception so Acme can pull redacted logs for forensic analysis? If so, can you confirm what fields would be included and whether any further pseudonymization is possible

3) Subprocessor transfers — Please provide your current US subprocessors and confirm whether any telemetry or logs are routed across state boundaries or to non-US subprocessors.

I've attached the initial Acme redline for reference (Acme_USPA_Redline_v1.docx).

Can you get back to us with proposed addendum language and the subprocessor list by EOD Monday? We have a broader procurement timeline to meet.

Best,
Maya Torres

Jordan / Priyom,

Quick technical recap and proposed language. TL;DR: we can sign as a Service Provider; telemetry exports are possible under a narrow, auditable workflow and with limits on fields retained.

Telemetry categories (what we collect by default):
- Request metadata: timestamp, request-id, model-id, latency bucket.
- Network metadata: source IP (last-octet truncated unless customer opts in), geolocation at region level, user-agent string.
- Runtime metrics: GPU allocation, token counts, error codes, trace ids.

Retention and pseudonymization notes:
- Default retention for telemetry is 30 days; 90 days available as an enterprise config.
- We can pseudonymize request-origin identifiers (hash+salt) for exported records and remove raw IPs from exports unless the customer requests raw IPs for a legal/incident reason. When raw IP export is requested, access is limited to a named SecOps contact and we create an audit entry.
- Subprocessors: AWS (us-east-1), FastStorage Inc. (US-based caching provider), LogPipe LLC (US log routing). None of the listed subprocessors transfer telemetry outside the US for Acme's account by default. For customers requiring contractually bounded routing, we can provide a region-locking option.

Proposed addendum paragraph (suggested wording for insert into Acme redline):

"Service Provider role and telemetry exports: Redwood Inference shall be deemed a Service Provider (or equivalent) with respect to Customer Content and processing performed to provide the Services. Redwood will not sell Personal Information. For operational purposes, Redwood collects telemetry necessary for service health and security. Upon Customer request for incident response or lawful investigative purposes, Redwood may provide an export of telemetry to Customer’s authorized security contacts subject to the following conditions: (a) telemetry exports will exclude raw Personal Information by default and will use pseudonymization (hashing with per-account salt) for request origin identifiers; (b) raw identifiers (including full IP addresses) will only be provided where Customer provides a documented lawful basis and names an authorized SecOps contact; (c) all exports are logged and retained in Redwood’s audit logs; and (d) Redwood will endeavor to route Telemetry within the United States for Customer accounts that require US-only data flows."

I'll attach a short CSV that maps field names to export behavior. If that language looks OK from a technical perspective, Priyom can make a legal polish pass.

—Vivek

Maya — thanks for the quick turn. Please find proposed addendum language below, reflecting the technical constraints Vivek outlined. In short: Redwood will sign as a Service Provider, will not sell Personal Information, and will support a narrow telemetry export exception for incident response under strict guardrails.

Proposed addendum text (for Acme’s redline):

"Service Provider designation; Telemetry exports. Redwood Inference shall act as a Service Provider with respect to Customer Content and shall not sell Personal Information. Redwood collects telemetry necessary for operation, monitoring, and security of the Services. At Customer’s written request for incident response or lawful investigative purposes, Redwood may provide telemetry exports to Customer’s designated SecOps contacts subject to the following: (1) exports will default to pseudonymized request-origin identifiers; (2) raw identifiers (including full IP addresses) will only be disclosed where Customer provides a written lawful basis and designates an authorized SecOps contact; (3) all export events will be recorded in Redwood’s audit logs and made available to Customer on request; (4) Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to keep telemetry routing and storage within the United States for Customer accounts that require US-only processing; and (5) Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of Subprocessors upon Customer request and before engaging any new subprocessors that materially change telemetry handling."

Attachments: I’ve attached a clean PDF of the draft addendum for your legal team (redwood-us-privacy-addendum-draft.pdf). We can accept redlines in DocuSign (link below) or a tracked-change Word if you prefer.
